sections.h2: Who bills and who values property in Hillsborough County?
sections.html:
The Hillsborough County Tax Collector bills and collects the tax, while the Hillsborough County Property Appraiser sets the values and decides exemptions. Both offices work from the county tax roll, so a question about your bill usually goes to one of them depending on whether it concerns value or payment.

The appraiser's main office is in the County Center at 601 E. Kennedy Boulevard in Tampa, on the 15th floor, open 8:00 am to 5:00 pm Monday through Friday at (813) 272-6100. Tax bills, payment options and a property tax search run through the tax collector's property tax page. Deeds and liens that affect a sale are filed with the clerk, covered on our Hillsborough County property records page.

  • Property Appraiser: value, homestead, Save Our Homes cap, portability, TRIM notice.
  • Tax Collector: bills, payments, installment plan, tax certificates.
  • Value Adjustment Board: hears value and exemption petitions.

sections.h2: When is Hillsborough County property tax due, and what are the discounts?
sections.html:
Hillsborough bills go out in November, are due November 1, and turn delinquent on April 1. The tax collector's FAQ says delinquent accounts pick up 3% interest plus advertising costs on that date.

The state calendar lets payers earn 4 percent off in November, 3 percent in December, 2 percent in January and 1 percent in February. March carries no discount. A payment that arrives after March 31 is late even if the bill was never opened, so sellers who list a house in winter should ask the title company to confirm which month's discount applies at closing.

Homeowners who want smaller payments can apply for the installment plan before May 1 of the tax year. The first payment is due in June. If June is missed, July still works but the discount is lost, and an account with no payment by July 31 is dropped from the plan. Full payment is then due in November with the 4 percent discount. Partial payments are accepted on current taxes under the tax collector's partial payment plan, and not on delinquent real estate taxes.

sections.h2: What dates matter on the Hillsborough County tax calendar?
sections.html:
Seven dates cover almost every Hillsborough County property tax decision, from the January 1 valuation to the April 1 delinquency.

Property tax calendar as printed by the Florida Department of Revenue and the Hillsborough offices
DateWhat happensSource
January 1Property valued; homestead status fixedFlorida Revenue
March 1Statutory deadline for exemption applicationsProperty Appraiser
May 1Last day to apply for the installment planTax Collector FAQ
Before June 1Tax certificate sale for delinquent accountsTax Collector FAQ
AugustTRIM notice mailed; value petition due within 25 daysFlorida Revenue
November 1Bills payableTax Collector FAQ
April 1Unpaid taxes delinquentTax Collector FAQ

The appraiser mails an Official Notice of Denial by July 1 when an exemption is refused, and that notice opens the right to a hearing before a magistrate hired by the Hillsborough County Value Adjustment Board.

sections.h2: What homestead and senior exemptions apply in Hillsborough County?
sections.html:
A Hillsborough County homeowner can deduct up to $50,000 from the assessed value of a permanent residence. The first $25,000 reduces every tax, and the second $25,000 applies to value between $50,000 and $75,000 and gives no break on the school tax.

After the first year, annual growth in assessed value is capped at the lower of 3 percent or the change in the Consumer Price Index. The appraiser says applications are taken year round, the statutory deadline is March 1, and a late application can be accepted up to the 25th day after the TRIM notice is mailed.

  • Low income senior exemption: the City of Tampa and unincorporated Hillsborough County allow up to $50,000, and Temple Terrace allows up to $25,000.
  • Long term resident senior exemption: offered by the City of Tampa and unincorporated Hillsborough County for homes with a just value under $250,000 and 25 consecutive years of residence.
  • Veterans, disabled, widowed and blind exemptions: documentation required; Hillsborough County Veterans Affairs is listed at 813-635-8316 for help with discharge papers.

An owner who keeps a homestead exemption after the house stops being the permanent home faces a lien for the exempted taxes from the prior 10 years, plus a 50 percent penalty and 15 percent interest, according to the appraiser. Report the change before a sale if the owner has moved out.

sections.h2: Does the 2026 Florida property tax amendment change the Hillsborough County homestead exemption?
sections.html:
The appraiser's legislative update page describes the amendment on the 2026 ballot as setting homestead exemption amounts of up to $150,000 beginning in 2027 and up to $250,000 beginning in 2028, and it directs the Legislature to schedule later increases. The appraiser's home page also carries a statement issued after the vote.

Ask the property appraiser how the amendment applies to your parcel and which taxes it reaches, because the legislative update page says the exact savings differ by property and cannot be calculated in advance. The Hillsborough County Tax Collector also posts a property tax reform page for the same ballot item. Until a bill shows a new exemption amount, plan a sale around the exemption printed on your current bill.

sections.h2: How is the tax handled when you sell a house in Hillsborough County?
sections.html:
The tax follows the property, so an unpaid Hillsborough County bill is settled at closing from the seller's proceeds. The tax collector notes that the name on the bill does not block payment, because the appraiser may not yet have received a recorded deed when the roll was certified.

A sale also ends the owner's homestead benefits. Florida treats any sale or transfer of title as a change of ownership, so the next January 1 the home is assessed at just value and the new owner has to apply again. Portability of the capped value belongs to the seller and attaches to a new homestead, not to the house being sold.

  • Escrowed loans: the servicer pays from a list sent to the tax collector, and after payoff the bill comes to the owner on or after November 1.
  • Documentary stamp tax: the state charges 70 cents per $100 of consideration on deeds in every county except Miami-Dade, and all parties to the deed are liable.
  • Portability: the new homestead must be established within three years of January 1 of the year the old one was abandoned, with Form DR-501T filed with the DR-501.

sections.h2: What happens if Hillsborough County property tax goes unpaid?
sections.html:
Unpaid tax leads first to a tax certificate and, after about two years, can lead to a tax deed sale. The tax collector runs the certificate sale as an online auction, with bidding that starts at 18 percent and drops in 0.25 percent steps, and the lowest rate wins.

The certificate is a first lien that ranks ahead of other government liens. The tax collector says an owner has up to 22 months after the certificate is issued before a tax deed foreclosure can begin, and the Florida statute counts two years from April 1 of the year of issue. Certificates on homestead parcels with under $250 due go to the county rather than to bidders. At the deed stage the clerk holds the auction, and an opening bid on homestead property includes one half of the latest assessed value.

A seller who is behind on tax still has time to sell. Paying the bill from closing proceeds redeems the lien and clears the title for the buyer.

faqs.q: When is Hillsborough County property tax due?
faqs.a: Bills are payable November 1 and become delinquent April 1. Payments made in November earn a 4 percent discount, December 3 percent, January 2 percent and February 1 percent. After the delinquency date, the tax collector adds 3% interest and advertising costs.

faqs.q: Can I pay Hillsborough County property tax in installments?
faqs.a: Yes, if you apply before May 1 of the tax year. The first payment falls in June. A July payment keeps you on the plan without the discount, and a missed July 31 deadline drops the account, which then owes the full amount in November with the 4% discount.

faqs.q: Who decides my Hillsborough County homestead exemption?
faqs.a: The Hillsborough County Property Appraiser decides it. The deadline is March 1, and a denial notice goes out by July 1 with a path to the Value Adjustment Board. The tax collector has no say over eligibility.

faqs.q: Does the tax collector accept partial payments on delinquent bills?
faqs.a: No. The tax collector accepts partial payments for current property taxes under a separate plan, but states that partial payments are not accepted for delinquent real estate taxes. Ask the office before sending less than the full balance.

faqs.q: What if I sell my Hillsborough County house before the bill arrives?
faqs.a: The tax still has to be settled at closing. The title company asks the tax collector for the amount due and pays it from the sale proceeds. The seller's homestead exemption ends with the sale, and the buyer applies for a new one by March 1 of the next year.
